batch_canonical.region: page 2, 10–62 % of the height — section 2, 'Опис на примероците'
batch_canonical.note: The page prints 'P05022' — SIX digits where every production lot in this record carries seven, so the laboratory's own line is short a digit. The laboratory's record is not the desk's to rewrite; which lot it certifies is a question of evidence, and five lines of it agree. The 227-М series runs 1 to 30 and maps one to one onto the thirty Tranche 3 retest certificates CoQ-PP_26-136 … 165. Twenty-nine of those numbers are already cited; the only one unused is 227-18. Exactly one certificate in that range carries no mycotoxin document at all: CoQ-PP_26-149, P050202, GP062501. The page names the strain Grape Pie, and GP062501 is Grape Pie. The only other Grape Pie lot a six-digit 'P05022' could be truncating is P050022, whose two certificates are numbered 007 and 095 and so lie outside this campaign entirely. The scan's own file name and the Drive audit of 20.09.2026 both read P050202 (GP062501). This is also the one certificate of the thirty that NOBODY could extract on 16.09.2026 — both readers failed on it then and both read it today.

name_aliases._region: page 2, 45–80 % of the height — the pesticide residue table
name_aliases._note: Two rows the two readers labelled differently while reporting the same result (н.д.). The page prints 'vkupno DDT', in Latin transliteration, and 'Endosulfan (alpha, beta and endosulfan sulfat)' — so read B is right on both and read A silently normalised the laboratory's own spelling: it rendered the transliteration back into Cyrillic and corrected 'sulfat' to 'sulfate'. That is precisely what the desk's standing rule forbids, because a laboratory's record is not ours to tidy. The first spelling listed in each pair is the page's; the rest are the readings folded onto it so the two reads can be compared row for row. No result is touched.
